Both REDs failed causally at their frozen tokens on genuine product paths (protocol: zero aggregate carriers among 1 legacy carrier/2 writers; browser: Bob's epoch-1 digest refused by predecessor-validation against displaced epoch 2), and the GREEN closes precisely those causes: the creator-signed `drp-creator-author-issuance-frontiers-state` carrier (canonical exact-key record, 8,192-byte ceiling with reproduced 6,241-byte maximum shape, Ed25519 signature verified against the independently authenticated successor floor, genesis pin, object/current/successor identity, ACL digests bound to anchor preimages, Cut/QC/manifest/prior-aggregate correlation, per-author monotone non-decrease in `authenticatedAggregatePair`, legacy-carrier equality, O(1) ref replacement in `creator-close.ts:950-977`) and the f4 exact pinned-genesis bootstrap predicate (sequence 0, epoch 0, pinned anchor, exactly `[pinnedGenesisAnchorDigest]` dependencies, logical time 1, exact object/author, digest/signature, byte-equal configured canonical operation), with slot zero excluded from covered-historical authority (`v3-live.ts:4741`) and the policy carried through hot adoption and cold reopen custody. The removed transition-side writer-set rederivation is honestly disclosed: the transition closure contains no detached successor ACL candidate, so frontier content is creator-attested and anchor-bound at open time, not independently rederived — this is not protection that exists and the plan does not claim it. The cross-object displaced-source target-derived bootstrap-policy field (`v3-live.ts:5068-5069`) is verified unconsumed (only `transportHandoff.displacedSource.*` at 7942-7943 is read, by the same-room handoff) and is not claimed as a verified cross-object path. Evidence is honestly scoped: 41/41 focused, exact two-title Chromium gate, 195/195 retained, builds/typechecks/lint/format/diff, and the signed isolated offline checkout at 9e1781e0/da3e7551 are represented accurately and disclaim general rebase safety, parent 0c1/0c closure, the >=100-transition gate, Phase-6 exit, and Phase-7 cold join. The f5 problem is real and source-confirmed: fresh-sequence reissue before source completion (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2950-2977`), adjacent-only prefix advance with permanent stall below a numeric gap (`creator-close.ts:526-535`), and four close-wide aborts (489, 517, 524, 528) that recur on retry because the offending vertex stays in the graph; ingress enforces no per-author prefix. For f5 I select the simpler construction from existing primitives: (A) per-author frontier freeze instead of close-wide aborts in `authorIssuanceFrontiersCandidate`, and (B) a second, disjoint recovery-side authority for above-boundary rows — RFC 9162 membership in the already creator-signed per-epoch `closeSetRoot`/`historyRoot` commitments (canonical `drp-history-leaf` entries; `inclusionProof`/`verifyInclusion`/`buildMerkleTree` already exported by `@ts-drp/compaction`, already a Node dependency), with the room's existing displaced-operation-identity dedup deciding complete-vs-reissue under current ACL/admission, and fail-closed per-author refusal when no admitted witness exists. The aggregate boundary is never advanced across a gap and no bare maximum is used. This needs no carrier/wire/schema/public-API/dependency/authority/threshold/migration change, so the f5 genuine-product-path tests-only RED under the amended causal matrix (both frozen tokens, null/absent/regression/duplicate mutants, restart, cold reopen, post-reopen issue/publish, green no-gap control) is authorized. No f5 production edit is authorized by this review.",

  "selected_design": "Two parts, both Node/room-internal over existing authenticated material. (A) Close liveness: in `authorIssuanceFrontiersCandidate` (packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:505-537), replace the four close-wide throws (duplicate slot 489, absent/null-prior first-observed>1 513-525, regression 527-529) with per-author dispositions that keep that author's frontier exactly at its prior value (or null/absent) and let the close proceed for all other authors; the anomalous vertex is never authenticated, no gap is crossed, and an unchanged retry succeeds because the same anomaly now yields the same frozen frontier instead of aborting. The aggregate record format, signing domain, 8,192-byte ceiling, sentinel rule, monotonicity checks, and transition normalization are unchanged. (B) Above-boundary settlement at recovery/rebase: the aggregate boundary keeps its exact current meaning (dense creator-observed prefix) and never crosses a gap; a local historical row with sequence above the boundary is authenticated as a settlement/reissue candidate iff the same author's later admitted vertex is proven a member of an authenticated closed epoch's close set — by deterministically rebuilding the epoch's canonical `drp-history-leaf` Merkle tree (leaf = {epoch, kind, objectId, ordinal, protocolMajor:3, vertexHash}; ordinal = authenticated previousHistorySize + index in the deterministic topological close order) from the writer's durable accepted-vertex journal and requiring root equality with the creator-signed CutValue `closeSetRoot` for that epoch (equivalently `verifyInclusion` against it), with the CutValue obtained from the already-authenticated anchor/trust/QC closure chain rather than from storage. The room's existing displaced-operation-identity dedup then decides complete-vs-reissue (match -> `completeRebaseSource`, no reissue; mismatch -> the row is only ever a fresh reissue candidate under the current ACL, admission policy, and canonical transformation), exactly the existing consumer contract. Rows above the boundary with no admitted witness (crash-before-reissue, held manual-review without completion, substituted/forked/replayed/cross-author/cross-object/cross-epoch rows) fail closed with a typed per-author refusal; the writer's own recovery may refuse, but the creator's close and all other authors are unaffected. The null-boundary error-code correction (finding 2) rides this slice.",
  "consumer_authority_contract": "`authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow()` (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4733-4795) grants exactly this: given the creator-signed aggregate identity for (objectId, author, boundary S, closedEpoch) — itself opened only from a verified successor-closure capability — a local durable row is classified covered-historical when it is nonzero-sequence, sequence <= S, epoch < closedEpoch, canonical-round-trip exact, digest-consistent between issued and outbox records, and Ed25519-verified under that author's own key. The classification yields only a reissue candidate: the row's operation is reduced to intents and reissued through the ordinary local-issue queue subject to the current ACL, the current admission policy, canonical transformation, and displaced-operation-identity deduplication; it never installs application state directly and never advances any frontier. Therefore the authenticated fact the consumer truly needs is 'this source row is done: either already represented by an admitted replacement or holding a terminal disposition' — not a per-sequence digest commitment from the creator. The existing close-set/history commitments (creator-signed CutValue closeSetRoot/historyRoot over canonical drp-history-leaf entries) already authenticate room admission of the replacement; the displaced-operation identity binds source to replacement at the room layer; the writer's own vertex signature binds the source. No heavier proof (per-gap creator receipts or a new accumulator) is required for this consumer or for later cold reopen, and none is selected.",
  "compatibility_boundary": "Frozen: no carrier/wire/schema/public-API/dependency/authority/threshold/migration change and no production edit in this checkpoint. The aggregate record, CutValue, history-leaf format, signing domains, latched-ACL 64-member cap (which matches the 64-entry frontier cap, so no capacity cliff exists), key schedules, and all immutable f2/f4 RED/GREEN evidence are unchanged. f5 GREEN may change only Node-internal close derivation and recovery/rebase classification plus room-internal orchestration, and only in directions that turn current aborts/refusals into per-author dispositions or proof-gated accepts; every new accept must be gated by the creator-signed trust chain and existing writer signatures. Proof material derives from the writer's durable accepted-vertex journal (existing product data, today unpruned); D.110c-c inherits the obligation that pruning never removes close-set leaves while a writer row still needs them, with fail-closed refusal as the fallback — no census or pruning rule changes here. Behavior for rooms without gaps or anomalies is bit-identical; the no-gap control must stay green.",
  "scope_preserved": true,
  "smallest_next_action": "Author the f5 genuine-product-path tests-only RED from a clean signed worktree: one noncreator writer with a known settled prefix retains two displaced rows, allocates intervening sequences so genuine rebase replacements land above the gap, runs at least two real close/adopt transitions, restarts, cold reopens, and attempts one post-reopen issue/publish (terminal `D110C_0C1F5_REBASE_SUPERSESSION_FRONTIER_REQUIRED`); plus the null-boundary offline-writer case and the absent/regression/duplicate mutants demonstrating the current close-wide aborts (terminal `D110C_0C1F5_FOREIGN_AUTHOR_CLOSE_LIVENESS_REQUIRED` after asserting current product outcomes), with the no-gap control green and exact old/new sequence/digest pairs and aggregate boundaries recorded. Sign and push the RED, then implement only the selected two-part construction and its mutants. The one bounded missing design fact f5 GREEN must resolve through the genuine product path: close-set leaf availability for a writer whose row was admitted while it was offline (journal completeness for the admitting epoch); the fail-closed per-author refusal is the acceptable fallback and requires no new authority, but if GREEN finds the genuine RED scenario itself needs successor-transferred close-set material, it must stop and reslice that as an explicit prerequisite rather than injecting tests-only durable state."
